insight.title: Why Speeding Up Can Make You Fall Behind
insight.subtitle: Why moving faster often pushes your goals further away.

sections.text: In space, accelerating toward a target in front of you is a mistake. Speeding up pushes you into a higher orbit, making your path longer and causing you to fall further behind your goal.
To reach your destination faster, you must decelerate. Dropping to a lower, tighter orbit is the only way to close the distance. In orbital physics, progress requires the discipline to slow down.
Rushing a decision creates "altitude"—extra complexity and errors that delay the final result. In your work, true progress often comes from lowering your altitude by stripping away the non-essential.
Try this today: When you feel the urge to rush a task today, stop and remove one unnecessary step.
Real momentum is found in the steps you choose not to take.
